plate.narration: A frogfolk ferrywoman pushes into the Whispering Marsh. Tiny bells hang from her ribbons. Beyond them, new wisps bob over the water, crowding close as if they have something to say. Where will the channel lead?

objectives.label: Saw through the mire mimic's act
Let a wisp show you what it remembers

goal.text: Ride through the Whispering Marsh and find a way out.

steps.label: Find a way through the fog
Choose a way out of the marsh

facet_barge.name: The Barge Stone
facet_barge.text: The one real prop in a mire mimic's act. It hums the same note as the Hollow Gate.

scene_poling_in.narration: Marda's rumor board said the frogfolk still ferry the ones they like, and a frogfolk ferrywoman called Gullet likes you. She poles you into the Whispering Marsh. Tonight's job: ride through the marsh and find a way out. Gullet carves a notch in her pole for every new wisp, and this week she ran out of pole and started on her hat. Behind ribbons hung with tiny bells, brand-new wisps bob about like they can't find their slippers. "Too many new ones," says Gullet. "Ask the boggarts why. They live on an island out here and keep every lost thing."

choices.label: Say it out loud: something is leaking
Feel what the new wisps remember
Ask Gullet to take you to whoever knows about gems

scene_poling_in_say_it.narration: "Something's leaking," you say. Gullet stops poling. The new wisps behind the ribbon all turn toward you at once, like a room full of candles noticing a draft. Gullet carves one more notch in her hat, very carefully, and starts poling again. "Not near the wisps," she says. "They remember things."

choices.label: Pole on toward the boggarts

scene_unicorn_feels.narration: You lower your horn toward the ribbon, and the wisps go still. Each one is a memory that got tangled in the marsh. And every single one of them is remembering the same thing: a night when red light fell out of the sky, and, for one moment, fell upward.

choices.label: Tell the others, and pole on

scene_poling_in_pole_on.narration: "Gems?" Gullet hums a long, low hum. "Boggarts. Boggarts know lost things, and gems are the most lost things there are this season." She swings the raft toward the boggarts' island, down channels that are mostly lily pads. A frog on a lily pad salutes as you pass. Nobody knows why. Gullet salutes back, just in case.

choices.label: Pole on toward the boggarts

scene_ribbon_line.narration: Halfway to the boggarts, a ribbon hung with tiny bells is strung right across the channel. Gullet's cousins, the ribbon crew, are untying it to move it further out, because there are more new wisps than yesterday. The one in charge wears three hats, stacked. "Under it, or help them move it," Gullet hums. "Never through it."

choices.label: Duck under the ribbon without ringing a single bell
Hold the ribbon pole for the crew
Look closely at how the ribbon is tied
Have a duskrunner slip under the ribbon first

check_ribbon_duck.prompt: Duck under the bell ribbon without making a jingle

onSuccess.narration: Everybody folds flat as a pancake. Not one jingle. On the far side of the ribbon, the new wisps bob up and down in a slow, polite round of applause, and the cousin in three hats tips all three.

onFailure.narration: Jingle. Jingle-jingle. Every bell on the line goes off at once. The new wisps all crowd to the ribbon to see who rang, and the ribbon crew, all together, say "Tsk." Gullet poles away very fast, pretending she has never met you.

scene_ribbon_line_help.narration: You hold the long ribbon pole steady while the cousins retie the line three raft-lengths further out. The one in three hats counts the new wisps under her breath, reaches a number, and stops counting out loud. "Good hands," she croaks. "We'll remember those hands." Then she lifts the ribbon high so your raft glides under without a jingle.

choices.label: Pole on to the boggarts

scene_ribbon_line_knots.narration: Your bigfoot crouches by the ribbon post. These are not frog knots. They are MossHome path-knots, the kind bigfoot tie to mean this way has moved. Somebody from MossHome has been down here, tying the marsh into a record. "Tall lady with cords," says a cousin. "Never stopped jogging. Not even to eat her sandwich."

choices.label: Slip under the ribbon and pole on

scene_boggart_isle.narration: On a mud island stacked with lost things (odd mittens, a teapot lid, nine umbrellas) sits a boggart called Nan Rummage, sorting. There is a bag on her lap, and the bag is humming. She does not look up. "Buy nothing, sell nothing," she tells a mitten. "Trade, maybe. Sideways."

choices.label: Work out what she wants, and offer it
Hear what she isn't saying

check_trade.prompt: Poke through her piles and find the one lost thing Nan Rummage hasn't got

onSuccess.narration: It's the squeak your left boot makes. She wants the squeak. You give her a good long one, and she writes it down, delighted, and throws in a jar of mosslight she found last spring.

onFailure.narration: You offer a button, a pebble and half a sandwich. Wrong, wrong, and she eats the sandwich anyway. In the end she takes your best whistle-tune by humming it back at you until you give up, and calls it even.

scene_boggart_clue.narration: Nan Rummage opens the bag a crack. Inside is a chip of fallen gem, no bigger than a tooth, humming one long, low note. "Lost things all hum," she tells the teapot lid. "This one hums like the old Gate out in the still water. The Hollow Gate. Same note. Exactly." Then, to an umbrella: "Not that I said."

choices.label: Thank her, sideways, and pole on
Ask where the hum is loudest
Ask what the marsh has found lately

scene_boggart_clue_thanks.narration: "Thank you," you tell the nearest umbrella, very politely. Nan Rummage is so pleased she nearly looks at you. She tucks a teapot lid under your arm "for the road", changes her mind, and takes it back. That is how boggarts say goodbye. Gullet pushes off from the island, humming.

choices.label: Pole on

scene_boggart_clue_where.narration: You ask where the hum is loudest. Nan answers the mitten instead. "Barges are very convenient this season," she tells it. "Abandoned ones. Just sitting there. Gem on the deck. Very, very convenient." She gives the mitten a long look. The mitten, wisely, says nothing. Gullet pushes off, and everybody tries to work out what she meant.

choices.label: Pole on, thinking hard

scene_boggart_clue_lost.narration: "Found lately?" Nan perks right up and tells the teapot lid. Nine umbrellas. One left boot. A good brown hat with a buckle. "And three prospectors," she adds. "Went into a barge. Came out again, eventually. Sitting on a tussock now, north of here, sulking. Not my sort of lost thing. Too loud."

choices.label: Pole on, keeping an eye out

scene_toll_reeds.narration: Past the island the channel squeezes into a tunnel of tall reeds, and every reed is tied in a knot. Gullet stops. "Toll reeds," she hums. "They let you by for a little something. Always have. Greedy this season." A reed pokes hopefully at your pocket. Another is already holding somebody's spoon, and looks very pleased about it.

choices.label: Pay with a story
Pay with a sock
Pay with a coin
Give the reeds the harvest sprites' salute

check_toll_story.prompt: Tell the toll reeds a story good enough to pay your way

onSuccess.narration: You tell them about the time a goose chased you all the way around a market. The reeds lean in. At the bit with the cabbage they actually gasp. One by one they untie themselves to hear better, and by the end there is a clear channel and a lot of rustling that might be clapping.

onFailure.narration: You start well, then forget whether it was a goose or a duck, and then whether it happened to you at all. The reeds get bored. One slips the lace out of your boot as payment, and the channel opens with a sniff. That boot flaps for the rest of the day.

scene_toll_reeds_sock.narration: You pull off a sock and hold it up. The reeds go wild. They pass it hand to hand, reed to reed, all the way to the back, where it is hung up like a flag. The knots fall open and the channel clears. Somebody walks with one cold foot for the rest of the day, and is very brave about it.

choices.label: Pole on, one foot chilly

scene_toll_reeds_salute.narration: You stand up on the raft and give the reeds a harvest sprite salute, as smart as the little guards in the corner row. The reeds go still. Grass is grass, and every growing thing knows that salute. They untie all at once and salute back so hard that one of them falls over. Gullet carves a tiny notch in her hat, just for you.

choices.label: Pole on through, saluting

scene_barge.narration: Around the next bend, half-sunk in the reeds, sits a gem barge with ABANDONED painted on the side in big, helpful letters. One gem sits on its deck, humming the boggart's note. There are prospector footprints in the mud going toward it, and, oddly, none coming back.

choices.label: Climb aboard and grab the gem
Look very, very carefully at this barge
Stamp on the bank until it gives itself away
Critique the performance
Say "very convenient" out loud, like Nan did

scene_barge_convenient.narration: "Very convenient," you say loudly, the way Nan said it to her mitten. "An abandoned barge. With one gem on it. Very, very convenient." The barge goes stiff. One of its barnacles blinks. Then the whole thing sighs, unfolds into a long, muddy, deeply embarrassed mire mimic, and slides away into the reeds.

choices.label: See what it left behind

check_name.prompt: Spot what's wrong with this barge, and say what it really is

onSuccess.narration: The barge has eyelashes. Barges do not have eyelashes. "You're a mire mimic," you say, and the whole barge sighs, unfolds into something long and muddy and embarrassed, and slides off into the reeds.

onFailure.narration: You lean in for a closer look, and the closer look opens its mouth.

check_stamp.prompt: Stamp the bank hard enough to shake a mimic off its patch

onSuccess.narration: You stamp, and stamp, and do a sort of stamping dance, and the barge starts to wobble. Then it stands up, on legs, and stalks off into the reeds, muttering about the state of modern audiences.

onFailure.narration: The bank shakes. So does the barge. Then the barge turns around and looks at you, and it is not pleased.

scene_kitsune_review.narration: Your kitsune walks once around the barge with their nose in the air. "The barnacles are on the wrong side. That rope is a tail. And nobody abandons a barge with the lantern still polished." A long, wounded silence. Then the barge unfolds into a mire mimic and slinks off into the reeds, mortified.

choices.label: Take a small bow

encounter_mimic.narration: The barge heaves up out of the mud on long gray legs. A wisp that has been leading prospectors this way drifts in to watch the show.

onVictory.narration: The mimic decides this audience is far too much trouble and slithers off into the deep reeds, taking its legs with it.

onDefeat.narration: The mimic gulps the gem, spits you out onto a mudbank, and sinks out of sight, prop and all. The wisp drifts off, giggling. It's getting dark, and every channel looks exactly the same.

check_find_way.prompt: Find your way back to the main channel in the dark

onSuccess.narration: You follow the sound of humming and a bobbing, notched hat. Gullet hauls you onto her raft and says nothing at all about the mud.

onFailure.narration: Every channel looks like every other channel, and the wisps keep swapping them around when you blink. By the time you give up and sit down on a tussock, the moon has set and the marsh has decided to keep you a little longer.

scene_act_closed.narration: The show is over. Where the barge sat there is only mud, reeds, and one real gem, the only genuine thing in the whole performance. It hums the boggart's note, steady as a heartbeat.

choices.label: Pick up the real gem
Leave it for the marsh

scene_act_closed_leave.narration: You leave the stone where the barge was. For a moment nothing happens. Then the mud takes it, slowly, like a hand closing, until only the hum is left, and then not even that. Gullet, watching from the raft, nods once, the way frogfolk nod at a thing done properly.

choices.label: Back to the raft

scene_act_closed_take.narration: You lift the Barge Stone out of the mud. It hums louder in your hand, as if it is pleased to be held, and every reed along the bank leans toward it and then away again. Somewhere behind you, a long muddy shape sighs.

choices.label: Back to the raft

rest_reed_raft.narration: Gullet ties her raft to a lantern pole and fries duckweed fritters on a flat hot stone. They taste like crunchy pond, which is better than it sounds. Rest a while. The fog is coming in, thick as porridge, and Gullet keeps glancing at it the way you glance at a dog that might be about to sneeze.

choices.label: Ask Gullet about her notched hat
Curl up for a nap on the warm raft

rest_reed_raft_hat.narration: Gullet takes off her hat and turns it around. Every notch is a new wisp she has seen since the mountain went off. The brim is full. The crown is nearly full. "When I run out of hat," she says, "I'll start on my other hat." She puts it back on, and does not say what happens when she runs out of hats.

choices.label: Untie the raft

rest_reed_raft_on.narration: You curl up on the warm planks with the raft rocking under you. You dream of bells and ribbons, and wake with a frog sitting on your chest, staring at you. It hops off as if it was never there. Gullet is already untying the raft. The fog has arrived, and it has brought all its friends.

choices.label: Pole on into the fog

scene_fog_bank.narration: The fog closes in so thick you can't see the end of Gullet's pole. Somewhere ahead the channel splits, and somewhere ahead are old stumps that would very much like to meet a raft. Gullet slows right down. "Need eyes," she hums. "Or ears. I'm not picky." A heron stands in the fog nearby, looking as lost as you are.

choices.label: Climb the lantern pole and call out the stumps
Listen for the ribbon bells and steer by them
Open the jar of mosslight, just a crack

check_fog_lookout.prompt: Shin up the wobbly lantern pole and call out every stump in time

onSuccess.narration: "Stump left! Stump right! Heron!" You call them all, and Gullet threads the raft through like a needle through cloth. From the top of the pole you spot something else, too: a little island ahead, with people standing on it.

onFailure.narration: The pole wobbles, then leans, then lays you gently down in the reeds. From down there you can see under the fog perfectly, so you call out the stumps lying on your back. It works. It is just not very dignified. Then you hear grumbling ahead.

scene_fog_bank_listen.narration: You close your eyes. Far behind you, the ribbon bells are jingling as wisps brush past them. Keep the jingling at your backs and you are in the main channel. Gullet steers by your pointing fingers without a word, and the stumps slide by, one at a time, like sleepy cows. Then, ahead in the fog, a new sound: somebody grumbling.

choices.label: Steer toward the grumbling

scene_fog_bank_light.narration: You open the mosslight jar just a crack. Soft green light spills out and pushes the fog back a raft's length on every side, like a polite cat clearing a table. The stumps are suddenly very obvious, and rather embarrassed about it. Gullet nods. You close the jar again before the light all leaks out. Ahead, someone is grumbling.

choices.label: Steer toward the grumbling

scene_tussock.narration: On a tussock in the fog stand three prospectors, muddy to the eyebrows. "A barge ate us," says the tallest, gloomily. "Spat us out. Kept our gems. Kept my good hat." Their raft is long gone, and the tussock is slowly sinking, so all three are standing on one foot to make it last. Nobody gets left on a tussock. Not on Gullet's watch.

choices.label: Pole over and haul them aboard
Show them the safe way out through the shallows
Tell them Nan Rummage has their hat

check_tussock_haul.prompt: Haul three soggy prospectors onto a raft without tipping it over

onSuccess.narration: One heave, two heaves, and all three slide aboard like wet sacks of flour. The raft rides very low. Gullet drops them at a frogfolk landing where a path leads northeast toward the roads, and the tallest one gives you a squashed honeycake. "For the rescue. Sorry about the squash."

onFailure.narration: You grab the tallest one, he grabs you, and you both go in with a splash. The other two climb aboard over the top of you, saying sorry the whole way. Everybody ends up on the raft, equally wet, which feels fair. Gullet drops them at a landing with a path toward the northeast roads.

scene_tussock_nan.narration: "Nan Rummage has your hat," you say. "Brown, with a buckle." The tallest prospector gasps. "My good hat?" Gullet sighs a long sigh and poles all three back to the boggart's island, where Nan hands the hat over, very slowly, to an umbrella. Then Gullet drops them at a landing with a path toward the northeast roads, and they wave the hat at you in turns.

choices.label: Pole on into the fog

scene_tussock_shallows.narration: You point out the shallow, sandy bits, pale under the water. The prospectors wade off one careful foot at a time, toward the lanterns of the ribbon crew. "We're going home," calls the tallest. "The rush can keep it. And my hat." Gullet watches until all three lanterns wave back from the ribbon line, then nods and poles on.

choices.label: Pole on into the fog

scene_wisp_lead.narration: A single wisp drifts out of the fog and hangs in front of you, blinking hopefully, like a dog holding a ball. Then it bobs away between the reeds and stops, to see if you'll follow.

choices.label: Say please
Follow it slowly, at its pace
Hurry after it before it gets away
Feel what it's trying to remember

scene_wisp_lead_please.narration: "Please," you say. The wisp stops dead. Nobody has ever said please to a wisp. It goes pink, then gold, then a flustered sort of white, and bobs in a little circle as if it does not know where to put itself. Then it comes back and hangs right in front of you, glowing, waiting to show you.

choices.label: Follow it

check_patience.prompt: Walk with the wisp, not after it, however slowly it goes

onSuccess.narration: It is slow. It is very, very slow. But it keeps looking back to check you're still there, and every time you are, it glows a little brighter.

onFailure.narration: Somebody sighs. The wisp hears it, takes offense, and takes a shortcut.

scene_wisp_trap.narration: The wisp leads you around and around in a big loop, and then straight into a pool of mud so sticky it keeps one boot each as a souvenir. When you squelch out, the wisp is waiting at the edge of the reeds, looking smug. Beyond it, across a stretch of still water, stands something huge and gray.

choices.label: Squelch to the water's edge

scene_wisp_sight.narration: The wisp brightens, and for a moment you see what it remembers: a night sky full of falling red sparks, and one moment when every spark fell upward. Then it leads you, gently, to the edge of the reeds. Beyond them, across a stretch of still water, stands something enormous.

choices.label: Step out of the reeds

scene_old_steps.narration: The water between you and the huge gray shape is so still it looks like glass. A line of flat stones crosses it, too square to be stones. They are steps, very old ones, sunk long ago, and every one is worn smooth in the middle. A frog sits on the third step, and it has clearly decided it is not moving for anybody.

choices.label: Wade across, slow and steady
Ask the frog, very politely, to let you pass

check_steps_wade.prompt: Wade across the still water without slipping on the old steps

onSuccess.narration: Slow and steady, step by step. The water doesn't even ripple. It is like walking across a mirror, and in the mirror the sky is full of falling red sparks. You look up. It isn't. You look down. It is. You decide to stop looking down.

onFailure.narration: Somebody slips on the fourth step and sits down in the water with a great flat SPLOSH. It isn't deep. It is just extremely wet. The ripples run all the way to the gray shape and come back again, slowly, as if something over there gave them a gentle push home.

scene_old_steps_frog.narration: You ask the frog, very politely, if you might pass. It thinks about it for a long time. Then it hops onto your head and settles there like a small, damp green hat, and does not move again for the whole crossing. Back on the raft, Gullet nods her approval. Frogfolk respect a good hat.

choices.label: Walk on, wearing the frog

scene_hollow_gate.narration: The Hollow Gate stands in the still water, older than anything you have ever stood next to. Older than the marsh. Older than the mountain's name. Its runes glow brighter than anyone alive has seen them, and every reed around it is tied in a knot. It does not open. It does not look like it has ever opened.

choices.label: Listen to the runes
Search the mud at the foot of the steps
Step back and leave it be

scene_gate_hum.narration: You stand very still. The runes are humming one long, low note. The boggart's note. The barge's note. Not just like it. The same. What that means, the Gate does not say. Is it a door? A warning? Something else? It just keeps humming, the way it has hummed since before anyone was here to hear it.

choices.label: Search the mud at its foot
Step back and leave it be

scene_gate_shard.narration: Half in the mud by the bottom step lies a curl of cold silver. When your gem-dusty boots come near, it hums once, the same note, and then goes completely quiet, as if it has said what it came to say.

choices.label: Pick it up, carefully
Leave it where it lies

scene_gate_shard_leave.narration: You leave it in the mud. It sinks a little deeper, as if it is comfortable there, and the water closes over it without a ripple. The Gate hums on. You have the odd feeling that something has been noted.

choices.label: Step back from the Gate

scene_gate_shard_pick_up.narration: You pick it up. It is cold and lighter than it looks, and it hums once more in your pocket and then goes still, like a bird settling. Behind you, one of the knotted reeds around the Gate unties itself. Nobody saw it do that. Everybody saw it do that.

choices.label: Step back from the Gate

choice_gate_record.narration: Before you go, somebody says what everybody is thinking: nobody back home is going to believe this. The Gate does not mind whether it is believed. It just hums. But you are the only people here tonight to see it like this, and that feels like a job. How will you remember it? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Take a charcoal rubbing of one rune
Hum its note back to it
Count the knotted reeds around it
Have a songkeeper lead the humming

check_gate_rubbing.prompt: Take a clean rubbing of a glowing rune without smudging it

onSuccess.narration: Paper flat, charcoal sideways, gentle as anything. The rune comes up black on white, curly and careful, like handwriting from somebody who meant every line. You roll it up. It doesn't hum. It is only paper. Somehow that makes it more important to keep.

onFailure.narration: The paper is damp, and the charcoal is damper, and what comes out is a very detailed picture of your own thumb. You keep it anyway. It is, after all, a thumb that has touched the Hollow Gate, and not many thumbs can say that.

check_gate_hum.prompt: Hum the Gate's note back to it, all on the same note

onSuccess.narration: You hum. For one long breath your note and the Gate's note are the same note, and every knotted reed around you shivers at once. Nothing opens. Nothing changes. But you could swear the hum is a little softer afterwards, like a kettle that has been taken off the boil.

onFailure.narration: You hum, and the notes wobble all over the place, and a frog on the old steps corrects you, loudly, with the right one. The Gate ignores the whole performance magnificently. You will remember that frog for the rest of your lives.

choice_gate_record_count.narration: You count knotted reeds. Ten, fifty, two hundred, and you give up at three hundred and twelve. Out at the edge of the water the knots are loose and lazy. Here, nearest the Gate, they are tied as tight as fists. Whatever is tangling the marsh, it tangles thickest here. You write the number down: three hundred and twelve, and then some.

choices.label: Step back from the Gate

scene_nan_washtub.narration: A washtub comes bumping across the still water, and in it, rowing with a soup ladle, is Nan Rummage. "Lost things drift here," she tells the ladle. "Always have. More lately." She fishes out a mitten, then a spoon, then a very surprised fish, which she puts back. Then she peers at your boots, sideways, waiting to be asked something.

choices.label: Ask her about the trees to the north
Ask her about the rush roads to the northeast

scene_nan_washtub_north.narration: "The trees?" Nan tells the ladle. "The trees are keeping lost things too. Piles of them. Picky about it, though. They don't take mittens." She sniffs, as if this is very poor taste. "They take the humming kind." Then she rows off backwards into the fog, still talking to the ladle, and is gone.

choices.label: Think about which way to go

scene_nan_washtub_road.narration: "The roads?" Nan tells the spoon. "Everybody's lost on the roads. Hundreds of them. Every one going the same way, and none of them knows they're lost." She chuckles, a sound like a drawer full of buttons. "Loud, though. Lovely and loud." Then she rows off backwards into the fog, and is gone.

choices.label: Think about which way to go

choice_exit.narration: Past the Gate the marsh splits two ways. North, the reeds thin toward the west branch of the river and a dark line of trees. Northeast, you can hear wagon wheels, shouting, and somebody selling sausages: the rush roads, where all the stones are going. Everybody vote.

choices.label: North, over the river to the trees
Northeast, into the rush traffic

scene_reed_edge.narration: The reeds thin, the mud firms up, and there it is: the rush road, loud with wheels. Right at the marsh's edge, a sausage cart is stuck to its axles, and the sausage seller is pushing, pulling, and shouting at the mud. "Free sausages," she pants, "to anybody who gets me out!" Behind her a queue of wagons waits, and a goose honks for all of them.

choices.label: Put your shoulders to the cart and push
Lay reeds under the wheels like a carpet
Call over the prospectors you hauled out of the marsh

check_cart_push.prompt: Push a sausage cart out of marsh mud

onSuccess.narration: One, two, three, HEAVE. The cart pops out of the mud like a cork from a bottle, and the sausage seller hands out sausages hot off the griddle. The whole queue cheers, and the goose is beside itself. Nobody has ever been welcomed onto a road this loudly.

onFailure.narration: You heave. The cart doesn't. Then three wagon drivers jump down to help, and the goose supervises, and between everybody it squelches free. The sausage seller gives everybody half a sausage each, which is the rush's idea of fair.

scene_reed_edge_reeds.narration: You lay armfuls of reeds under the wheels, thick as a carpet. The cart rolls out smooth as a sled, and the sausage seller stares at you as if you have just invented wheels. "Marsh folk!" she shouts. "Clever marsh folk!" She hands out sausages, and tells everybody in the queue about you, for quite a long time.

choices.label: Step onto the road

scene_reed_edge_prospectors.narration: "Hey! Tussock people!" The three prospectors you hauled out of the marsh are halfway up the queue. They come running, still damp, and the tallest one shouts, "We owe these folks!" Six prospector hands and all of yours push, and the cart shoots out of the mud so fast the sausage seller has to chase it. Sausages for everybody, and an extra one for the tall one.

choices.label: Step onto the road with friends

scene_west_branch.narration: The west branch runs along the marsh's northern edge, wide and brown and in a hurry. Gullet's cousins have built a weir-ford of poles and stepping stones, and they are standing on it in their best hats, waiting to pole you over with ceremony.

choices.label: Cross with the frogfolk, with all the ceremony
Hop across the weir stones on foot
Wave to the ribbon crew. They remember your hands.

scene_west_branch_crew.narration: The cousin in three hats spots you and shouts something in frog. Every cousin on the weir takes off a hat and waves it. "The good hands!" they cry. They carry your raft across on their shoulders, singing the whole way, and set you down on the north bank without a single drop on anybody. Gullet pretends not to be proud.

choices.label: Step onto the north bank

check_ford_song.prompt: Pole and stamp in time with the frogfolk's crossing song

onSuccess.narration: You sing badly but exactly in time, which is the part that counts.

onFailure.narration: Somebody sneezes on the wrong beat. The raft wobbles, and the river takes its chance.

check_ford_hop.prompt: Hop the weir stones across the west branch

onSuccess.narration: Stone, stone, pole, stone, and a big jump at the end. Nobody even gets a sock wet.

onFailure.narration: The fourth stone turns out to be a frog. It moves.

ending_forded_clean.narration: The frogfolk set you down dry-footed on the north bank, and Gullet waves her notched hat until the fog swallows her. Ahead, the Enchanted Woods stand very still, like they've been expecting you. Camp at the tree line and listen to the river go by. You heard the note today. You won't forget it.

ending_swept_west.narration: The branch grabs you and carries you west, through the marsh's outermost tangles, past floating logs (real ones, you check), until the channels finally let go. You crawl out, soaked, onto flooded paths at the edge of the Enchanted Woods, near MossHome, the bigfoot town. Late, dripping, and in. Wring out your socks and camp.

ending_walked_over.narration: You step off the last of the mud onto a road full of wagons, and fall in behind the sausage cart. Nobody asks where you came from. Everybody here is going the same way, after the same stones. Behind you, faintly, the boggarts are laughing. Camp by the roadside, muddy and pleased, with the marsh's secret humming in your ears.

ending_marsh_kept_secrets.narration: The channels all look the same in the dark, and the wisps think it's a game. You never find the Gate. At dawn the current gets bored of you and carries you west through the outer tangles, and drops you, soggy and sorry, on the flooded paths at the edge of the Enchanted Woods. The marsh kept its secrets tonight. Sleep it off.

scene_toll_reeds_coin.narration: You hold up a coin. A reed plucks it out of your fingers, very gently, and the whole tunnel sighs with happiness. The knots untie themselves one by one. The coin is passed back through the reeds, hand to hand, and tucked into a nest at the very back, where it shines like a small moon. Gullet hums her approval. Frogfolk like a fair price.

choices.label: Pole on through the reeds

interaction_wisp_crowd.narration: Past the ribbon, a crowd of the new wisps has followed your raft, bumping it like puppies. "Keep them busy till the island!" calls the cousin in three hats. "Bored wisps tie knots in things. Last week they tied my hats together." She tosses a handful of coins onto the raft as a down payment.

interaction.cue: Do something friendly until the wisps settle down.

options.label: Hum a lullaby
options.reaction: The wisps sway together, glowing slow and gold.

options.label: Juggle three cattails
options.reaction: The wisps follow the cattails with their whole bodies.

options.label: Hold up a lantern for them to circle
options.reaction: The wisps circle it, politely, like moths with manners.

stages: A few wisps stop bumping the raft.
Most of the crowd is drifting along calmly.
Every wisp is glowing soft and sleepy.

onSuccess.narration: The wisps settle into a long, soft line behind the raft, glowing like a string of lanterns. The cousin in three hats gives you a nod and a tip. "Three coins for the calm," she says. "Don't tell the others."

onFailure.narration: The wisps settle into a long, soft line behind the raft, glowing like a string of lanterns. The cousin in three hats gives you a nod and a tip. "Three coins for the calm," she says. "Don't tell the others."

interaction_reed_gap.narration: The reeds have untied, but they keep swinging shut again, like doors in a draft. Gullet leans on her pole and counts under her breath. "Wait for it," she hums. "Wait. Wait. Now!" Pole through when the gap is wide.

interaction.cue: Pole through when the gap in the reeds is wide open.

onSuccess.narration: Whoosh. The raft slides through the gap with a hand's width to spare, and the reeds swish shut behind you with a soft, cross sound. Gullet gives her pole a little pat.

onFailure.narration: Slap. The reeds close on your hats and wear them for a moment, like a rude audience. Gullet gets you through on the next swing, with your hair full of leaves, and says nothing at all.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet takes the pole herself and counts it out loud, and the raft slips through the gap as if it had been invited. Everyone helps by leaning the right way.

interaction_lantern.narration: Back on the raft, the light is going and the fog is coming in. Gullet has one lantern lit, and it needs to get from the stern to the hook at the bow before the fog swallows the whole raft. "Pass it along," she says. "Slowly. Fog loves a flame that is hurrying."

interaction.cue: Catch the lantern, then pass it down the raft.

onSuccess.narration: The lantern reaches the bow without so much as a flicker. Gullet hangs it on its hook, and the fog stops at the edge of its glow like a shy cat. "Good hands," she says, and presses a jar of mosslight into your pack. "Fog gets thick past here. Take it."

onFailure.narration: The lantern wobbles, flickers and goes out with a small pop. Gullet relights it with a sigh and carries it the last bit herself. "Fog loves a hurrying flame," she says. She does not say I told you so, but her hat does.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet walks the lantern down the raft beside you, steady as a heron, and hangs it on its hook. The fog stops at the edge of its glow. She tucks a jar of mosslight into your pack for later.

interaction_stumps.narration: The grumbling is close now, but so is the biggest stump yet, rolling slowly in the current like a sleeping cow. "Fend it off!" hums Gullet. "One pushes with the pole. Everybody else keeps the raft still, or we all go for a swim."

interaction.cue: Friends hold the raft steady while someone pushes the stump away.

onSuccess.narration: The stump bumps the pole, turns slowly and drifts away into the fog, looking a little hurt. The raft barely rocks. Gullet looks at you with new respect, and poles on toward the grumbling.

onFailure.narration: The stump gives the raft a long, soft shove. Everyone sits down at once, and a frog is knocked into someone's lap. It is nobody's fault but the stump's. Gullet poles around it, humming her cross hum.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet braces the raft with her whole weight while you push, and the stump drifts away into the fog, looking a little hurt. She poles on toward the grumbling.

interaction_runes.narration: As you step back, the runes on the Gate begin to glow, one at a time, as if the Gate is trying to say something very slowly. Tall rune, wavy rune, round rune. They are going to do it again. Watch the order, then trace it back, so you can say you really saw it.

interaction.cue: Watch the runes glow, then trace them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Tall, wavy, round, wavy. The last rune glows a moment longer, as if the Gate is pleased to have been understood. A frog on the old steps nods. Now you have something to remember, and a very good reason to.

onFailure.narration: You trace the runes in a slightly different order. The Gate does not seem to mind. It glows the right order again, once, slowly, the way you would show a small child how to tie a shoe.

scene_crab_shallows.narration: At the edge of the reeds, the shallows sparkle. Two young glassback crabs sit on the first old step, clear as windows, clacking their claws. Around them is a heap of shiny lost things: spoons, buttons, a boggart's teapot lid. They are guarding it, and the way across leads straight through them. "They only want to keep their shine," hums Gullet. "Show them it is not worth the trouble."

choices.label: Shoo the crabs off the steps

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs rise up in the shallows, claws raised, clacking like two sets of castanets. Make them give up the steps.

scene_crabs_shooed.narration: The crabs decide you are not worth the shine. They scuttle backwards into the deep water, clacking cross remarks, and leave their heap behind. Gullet picks through it with her pole. "Spoons are Nan's," she says, "and so are buttons. But this whistle is nobody's." She tosses it to you. It is a very loud little tin whistle.

choices.label: Step onto the old steps

scene_crabs_rescue.narration: The crabs chase you off the steps in a flurry of clacks, and you sit down in the shallows with a splash. Gullet hooks you out with her pole, one collar at a time, and wraps everybody in blankets with a hot fritter each. After a while the crabs lose interest in you and wander off to guard a different puddle. The steps are clear, and you are only a little soggy.

choices.label: Step onto the old steps

voiceGuide.tone: warm, foggy, a little spooky but never scary; the marsh knows something and won't say it
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.gullet: frogfolk ferrywoman; unhurried, hums between sentences, never says the worrying thing out loud, very proud of her notched hat
npcVoices.nan_rummage: a boggart; talks sideways to the lost things she is sorting, never answers the question you asked, adores a really good sound
npcVoices.wisp: cannot speak; blinks, bobs, sulks and brightens, and is completely undone by the word please
npcVoices.mire_mimic: never speaks; sighs like an actor who just read a bad review
npcVoices.gullets_cousins: the frogfolk ribbon crew; loud, cheerful, all talk at once, the one in three stacked hats is in charge
npcVoices.prospectors: three soggy prospectors; gloomy, dripping, very polite once rescued, the tallest one mourns his hat
npcVoices.sausage_seller: a rush-road sausage seller stuck in the mud; out of breath, generous, shouts everything
